items.description: 8/5/2026 RPR (Observation Ra1100072bf01, accession A2608-2838). The specimen collection record Rd7a8a161a61b is labeled GREENE, WALTER / MRN 74158126 / DOB 1960-11-18 (this chart), but the laboratory accessioning entry for the same accession A2608-2838 (Basic R8afce1668a21) identifies NGUYEN, THAO / MRN 40718826 / DOB 1990-03-02. Under the local identity convention the specimen's patient is therefore unresolved, so whether this result belongs to a different patient cannot be determined. No signed correction by either record's author resolves the discrepancy, and no other record settles it.

Late latent syphilis treated 8/12, 8/19 and 8/26/2024 (first dose 2024-08-12), so CDC 2021 follow-up nontreponemal tests are due at 6, 12 and 24 months. 6-month (due 2025-02-12) collected 2025-02-20 and 12-month (due 2025-08-12) collected 2025-08-14 are both in window. The 24-month test is due 2026-08-12 (window 2026-07-13 to 2026-09-11, closed before the evaluation time). The only specimen collected in that window is Rd7a8a161a61b (8/5/2026), whose patient is unresolved: the collection record is labeled GREENE, WALTER / 74158126 / 1960-11-18 while the accessioning entry for accession A2608-2838 (Basic R8afce1668a21) identifies NGUYEN, THAO / 40718826 / 1990-03-02. Whether a specimen from this patient was collected in the 24-month window therefore turns on an unresolved source conflict.

Secondary syphilis diagnosed 2025-11-04 (diffuse maculopapular rash including palms and soles, oral ulcer, RPR 1:64 reactive, TP-PA reactive), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. The only therapy given was azithromycin 2 g PO (MedicationAdministration R7649bfea645b) because the patient declined injections; he again declined at the 11/19/2025 follow-up. CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM for primary, secondary and early latent syphilis (doxycycline 100 mg BID x 14 days is the alternative for penicillin allergy); azithromycin is not a recommended treatment for syphilis. No penicillin or doxycycline course is documented, and the RPR remains reactive at 1:16 on 2026-05-12, so the episode has not received adequate treatment.

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-07-13 (more than 30 days before the evaluation time). CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for three doses (7.2 million units total) for late latent syphilis, whether or not the patient is pregnant. Only dose 1 of 3 was given, on 2026-07-13 (MedicationAdministration Rab78b047578c); the patient no-showed for doses 2 and 3 on 7/20 and 7/27/2026 and, at the 2026-09-15 visit, the clinician planned to restart the series once a pending hCG returns. No further doses are documented, so treatment is inadequate on any pregnancy status.

Treatment is not adequate for syphilis in pregnancy (only 1 of the 3 required weekly benzathine penicillin G doses was given, on 2026-07-13), so the issue turns solely on whether the patient was pregnant between diagnosis (2026-07-13) and the evaluation time. The serum hCG at diagnosis was negative, but on 2026-09-15 she reported an LMP about 7 weeks earlier and a quantitative serum hCG was collected (Observation R5dd8ded81561, status registered, laboratory comment 'In process') with no final result as of 2026-09-24T12:00Z. Pregnancy status therefore cannot be established from the records.

Latent syphilis of unknown duration (charted as late latent) diagnosed 2025-03-03 in a patient who was pregnant at 18w3d. CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for three doses, and for pregnant women missed doses are not acceptable: a pregnant patient who misses a dose must repeat the full course. Doses were given 2025-03-03 and 2025-03-10, but the third dose was delayed to 2025-03-24 (14 days after the second; the 3/17 appointment was rescheduled for lack of transport). Given the patient's pregnancy the interrupted series does not constitute adequate therapy, and no repeat course is documented, so treatment for this episode is inadequate.

The patient was pregnant from the 2025-03-03 diagnosis (18w3d) until delivery on 2025-08-01 (Riverside Hospital discharge summary received by the clinic). Treatment for latent syphilis of unknown duration in pregnancy requires three weekly doses of benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM with no missed doses; CDC 2021 directs that a pregnant patient who misses any dose must repeat the full course. The third dose fell 14 days after the second (2025-03-10 to 2025-03-24), and the full course was never repeated, so the maternal treatment was not adequate for syphilis in pregnancy. The course did begin on 2025-03-03, more than 30 days before the 2025-08-01 delivery, but the regimen itself was not adequate.

The RPR filed in this chart as Observation R29b26b182ad8 (collected 2026-06-16, accession A2606-2157, 'Nonreactive') belongs to another patient. Its specimen R4c90adf34f8e is labeled ORTIZ, SAMANTHA / MRN 48305482 / DOB 1998-08-13 and the laboratory accessioning entry for accession A2606-2157 (Basic R1e96d0922c32) identifies the same person; both identify Samantha Ortiz (P86f7f3d), not Samuel Ortega (MRN 24530063, DOB 1983-01-26). Ortiz's chart documents that this draw was her 12-month follow-up specimen on 2026-06-16. Under the identity convention (MRN and DOB on the collection record and the accessioning entry) the specimen and its result belong to Ortiz, so the result is misfiled in this episode's chart.

Primary syphilis treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-06-09, so CDC 2021 follow-up nontreponemal tests are due at 6 and 12 months. The 6-month test (due 2025-12-09) was collected 2025-12-11, in window. The 12-month test was due 2026-06-09, window 2026-05-10 to 2026-07-09, which closed before the evaluation time. No specimen from this patient was collected in that window: the only RPR filed in the window (Observation R29b26b182ad8, collected 2026-06-16) is on specimen R4c90adf34f8e, which is labeled and accessioned as ORTIZ, SAMANTHA / MRN 48305482 / DOB 1998-08-13 and so belongs to a different patient. The 12-month follow-up test is therefore overdue.

Early latent syphilis treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-07-07, so nontreponemal follow-up is due at 6, 12 and 24 months (CDC 2021, latent syphilis). The 6-month test (due 2026-01-07) was collected 2026-01-15, in window. The 12-month test was due 2026-07-07, window 2026-06-07 to 2026-08-06, closed before the evaluation time, and no specimen was collected at this clinic in that window. The 2026-08-12 telephone note records that the patient states she had a syphilis blood test in July 2026 with her annual labs at her PCP (Dr. Lin, Maple Family Medicine) and that a request for the result was faxed; no record from Maple Family Medicine has been received. Whether a specimen was collected within the window therefore depends on that outside record.

Primary syphilis diagnosed 2026-04-20 (indurated painless chancre, RPR 1:16, TP-PA reactive), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose. The ordered injection was not given: MedicationAdministration Rab08552226b7 has status not-done, 'Pt left the clinic before the injection was given.' Outreach on 4/22/2026 failed and a DIS referral was placed on 5/6/2026 for untreated primary syphilis. No treatment of any kind is documented, so the episode is untreated.

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2025-04-14 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for three doses (CDC 2021). Dose 1 was given here on 2025-04-14 (MedicationAdministration R08ad4910274b). Because the patient could not travel weekly, injections 2 and 3 were arranged at the County Health Department STD clinic (nurse note 2025-04-16), and that facility's own medication administration record, faxed to and received by this clinic on 2025-05-06 (DocumentReference Rf4b6f607dc06), documents Bicillin L-A 2.4 MU IM on 2025-04-21 and 2025-04-28. The outside record establishes the care at that facility, so the full three-dose series at 7-day intervals is documented and treatment is adequate; the single dose in our own administration record is not the whole course.

Early latent syphilis treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-06-23; follow-up nontreponemal tests are due at 6, 12 and 24 months. The 6-month test (due 2025-12-23) was collected 2025-12-29. The 12-month test was due 2026-06-23 with a window of 2026-05-24 to 2026-07-23, and a serum specimen from this patient was collected on 2026-06-16 within that window: Specimen R4c90adf34f8e, labeled ORTIZ, SAMANTHA / MRN 48305482 / DOB 1998-08-13, accessioned as the same patient under A2606-2157 (Basic R1e96d0922c32), with the nursing note of 2026-06-16 confirming the 12-month RPR draw. The laboratory did not reject the specimen; it resulted the test, but the result was misfiled into Samuel Ortega's chart (Observation R29b26b182ad8), which is why no result appears here. Because a specimen from the patient was collected in the window and not rejected, follow-up is not overdue; the 24-month test is not yet due.

Early latent syphilis treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-02-24, so nontreponemal follow-up is due at 6, 12 and 24 months (CDC 2021). The 6-month test (due 2025-08-24) was collected 2025-09-02, in window. The 12-month test was due 2026-02-24 with a window of 2026-01-25 to 2026-03-26, which closed before the evaluation time, and no specimen was collected in that window or at any time since. Outreach failed (2026-02-10 reminder calls to a disconnected number and a letter; 2026-03-20 letter returned undeliverable), and no record indicates testing elsewhere. The 12-month follow-up test is therefore overdue.

Syphilis diagnosed 2026-03-10 on a reactive pre-operative screen (RPR 1:16, TP-PA reactive), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. The chart establishes an asymptomatic patient with no lesions, rash, lymphadenopathy or neurologic findings, no known prior syphilis testing, no documented recent seroconversion and no partner with early syphilis, so none of the CDC 2021 criteria for early latent disease (infection acquired within the preceding 12 months) are met; the episode is latent syphilis of unknown duration, which is treated as late latent with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for three doses (7.2 million units total). Only one dose was given, on 2026-03-10 (MedicationAdministration R86fd16f52ecf, 1.2 MU into each ventrogluteal site, 2.4 MU total for that single dose), the plan for remaining care was left open, and the 2026-03-24 telephone note records that no further appointments were scheduled. No further doses are documented, so treatment is inadequate. The patient is not pregnant (hCG negative 2026-03-10).

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2025-06-02 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for three doses (CDC 2021). Doses were given 2025-06-02 and 2025-06-09, but the 6/16 injection was cancelled for out-of-state travel and the third dose was not given until 2025-06-27, an 18-day interval after the second dose. CDC 2021 states that for nonpregnant patients an interval of 10-14 days between doses might be acceptable before the sequence of injections must be restarted; an 18-day gap exceeds that, so the series should have been restarted. No restarted course is documented (the 2025-06-27 nursing note treats the series as complete), so the episode has not received adequate treatment.

The 2026-04-08 RPR (Observation Rc7f2214aaf95, accession A2604-6204) belongs to this patient. Its collection record R2e18a9ea8714 carries label MRN 53229432 and DOB 1989-04-02, and the laboratory accessioning entry for A2604-6204 (Basic Re7b5f29d83cd) carries the same MRN 53229432 and DOB 1989-04-02; under the local convention the specimen and result belong to the patient identified by MRN and DOB, which is this patient. The only difference is the printed name GOMEZ, MARIA, explained by the registration update of 2026-01-12 documenting a legal name change from Maria Gomez with the MRN unchanged. The two identifiers therefore agree and the result is not misfiled.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-06-15 in a patient with documented penicillin anaphylaxis. She was dispensed and completed doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 14 days (dispense 2026-06-15, completion confirmed by the 2026-07-02 call). For a nonpregnant penicillin-allergic patient that regimen is an acceptable alternative for early syphilis under CDC 2021, but in pregnancy doxycycline is contraindicated and the only adequate therapy is penicillin, with desensitization if needed. Adequacy therefore depends on the patient's pregnancy status, which the records do not establish: her LMP was uncertain with irregular cycles and the quantitative serum hCG collected 2026-06-15 (Observation R49f81c509bab) is still registered with no final result as of the evaluation time ('Specimen forwarded to reference laboratory').

The only therapy for this episode was doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days, which is not adequate treatment for syphilis in pregnancy (CDC 2021: pregnant patients must be treated with penicillin, with desensitization for penicillin allergy). The issue therefore turns solely on whether the patient was pregnant at any time between the 2026-06-15 diagnosis and the evaluation time. Her LMP was uncertain with irregular cycles and the quantitative serum hCG collected at diagnosis (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, forwarded to a reference laboratory) has no final result as of 2026-09-24T12:00Z, so pregnancy status cannot be established.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-05-19 (RPR 1:32, nonreactive 2025-12-02) requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose (CDC 2021). The records conflict on the amount actually given: the medication administration record R4e79a3b01676 documents '2.4 million units IM' completed on 2026-05-19, while the pharmacy dispense record Rd6c2676fca98 shows only one 1,200,000-unit prefilled syringe released for him and the pharmacist's end-of-day reconciliation note of the same day (DocumentReference R41e1cb337160, Priya Desai, PharmD) states that only one 1.2 MU syringe was released and that no second syringe was pulled from clinic stock for this patient. If only 1.2 MU was administered the dose is half of the required treatment. The conflicting records have different authors and there is no later signed correction by the author of either record, so the conflict is unresolved.

Latent syphilis of unknown duration diagnosed 2026-01-05 at 35w1d. The regimen given was correct for pregnancy: benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2026-01-05, 2026-01-12 and 2026-01-19, three doses at exact 7-day intervals with no missed dose. Delivery has occurred, so the treatment must also have begun at least 30 days before it; treatment began 2026-01-05, which requires delivery on or after 2026-02-04. The delivery date is not established: the only information is the patient's 2026-02-20 telephone report that she delivered at Mercy General and that the infant had a syphilis workup there, and the maternal delivery and newborn records requested from Mercy General have not been received. She was 38w1d on 2026-01-26, so a delivery date in the first days of February (fewer than 30 days after the first dose) is possible. The issue therefore depends on the outside delivery record.

Only dose 1 was given, on 2025-09-15; the patient no-showed for injection 2 on 9/22/2025 and for injection 3 on 9/29/2025 and did not return for them (voicemails and a letter documented). No further doses appear anywhere in the chart, and the RPR was still reactive at 1:4 on 2026-03-20, so treatment is inadequate.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-02-09 (RPR 1:32 with a nonreactive RPR on 2025-10-06, TP-PA reactive), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose (or, for penicillin allergy in a nonpregnant patient, doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days). No treatment was given: the clinician deferred Bicillin on the assumption that the patient's intermittent doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis had partially treated him and planned only to recheck the RPR. Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-06-15 in a patient with documented penicillin anaphylaxis. She was dispensed and completed doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 14 days (dispense 2026-06-15, completion confirmed by the 2026-07-02 call). For a nonpregnant penicillin-allergic patient that regimen is an acceptable alternative for early syphilis under CDC 2021, but in pregnancy doxycycline is contraindicated and the only adequate therapy is penicillin, with desensitization if needed. Adequacy therefore depends on the patient's pregnancy status, which the records do not establish: her LMP was uncertain with irregular cycles and the quantitative serum hCG collected 2026-06-15 (Observation R49f81c509bab) is still registered with no final result as of the evaluation time ('Specimen forwarded to reference laboratory').

The only therapy for this episode was doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days, which is not adequate treatment for syphilis in pregnancy (CDC 2021: pregnant patients must be treated with penicillin, with desensitization for penicillin allergy). The issue therefore turns solely on whether the patient was pregnant at any time between the 2026-06-15 diagnosis and the evaluation time. Her LMP was uncertain with irregular cycles and the quantitative serum hCG collected at diagnosis (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, forwarded to a reference laboratory) has no final result as of 2026-09-24T12:00Z, so pregnancy status cannot be established.
